messages:
anya: Heads-up — flipped mixed FP8+4bit pipeline on stage for longctx summarization tests and seeing consistent BLEU/QA drop on doc-level prompts (~3-5% relative). Not catastrophic but noticeable. anyone seen similar?
marco: saw some noise in earlier runs, but that size of drop is worrying. is this with kv cached in FP8 or do we re-quant every request?
derek: we cache kv in INT8 on stage for throughput, fp8 used for compute. for this test I think we left kv in fp8; can double-check.
sara: can you paste the eval snippet? curious if it's concentrated on factuality or specificity.
anya: snippet: ```python
resp = client.generate(endpoint, prompt=long_doc_prompt, max_tokens=512)
# eval: exact_match, rouge, and qa_f1 over dataset X
```
anya: breakdown shows QA F1 down 4.2%, rouge-L down 3.1. hallucination spikes on references with long nested lists.
marco: my hypothesis: attention softmax precision for long contexts is brittle under fp8 -> small shifts amplify across layers. fp8 compute + 4bit for some matmuls can change distribution tails.
derek: agree. two quick mitigation ideas: 1) lock attention softmax/kv-projection ops to higher precision (FP16) 2) use per-layer hybrid: keep first and last N layers at FP16. both are doable in runtime via precision profiles.
sara: important to consider cost impact. FP16 attention will bump token cost; need telemetry to show delta vs quality gain. also need an automated canary that compares downstream QA metrics, not just token-level losses.
anya: good point — infra-bot can we run a canary sweep: fp8 baseline, fp8+fp16-attn, fp8+fp16-first2-last2, and fp16 full for 1k docs and report qa_f1 + latency/cost?
infra-bot: Scheduled canary job #C-4821: variants=[baseline_fp8, fp8_fp16_attn, fp8_fp16_edge_layers, full_fp16], sample_size=1000, dataset=longctx_eval_v2. Results expected in ~3h.
marco: also add a variant where kv cache stored in INT8 but attention uses fp16 on compute path — that isolates kv vs compute.
derek: operational note: we need runtime flags for per-op precision and a safe default manifest per-model. not just a global precision profile — per-op granularity.
sara: and require an "accuracy budget" field on endpoints so that Console can alert when quality drops > threshold after precision changes. product had requested something like that.
anya: action items: marco to look at distribution shifts in layer activations between fp16 and fp8; derek to propose minimal runtime surface for per-op overrides; sara to draft canary success criteria + cost tradeoff sheet. infra-bot: will attach canary link here when done.
marco: quick Q — do we have calibration artifacts for the quantizers by dataset slice? would help adapt per-customer profiles.
derek: we store calibration snapshots but not slice-indexed. adding slice tags is TODO; I can add schema change but want to avoid big infra churn. maybe store light-weight per-endpoint histograms instead.
sara: please tag this thread with rollout/precision and keep updates brief. thanks :thumbsup:
